beats.title: Squash Is Farmed in Oaxaca
beats.description: Foragers in a Mexican cave began growing squash, among the first domesticated crops of the Americas.

beats.title: Cacao Is Drunk in the Amazon Edge
beats.description: People of the upper Amazon in Ecuador used cacao, the earliest known use of the plant that gives us chocolate.
beats.note: Search: about 5,300 years ago at Santa Ana-La Florida

beats.title: Caral Rises in the Peruvian Desert
beats.description: Pyramids and plazas went up in a river valley of Peru, in one of the oldest cities anywhere in the Americas.
beats.note: Approximate start of the main building phase

beats.title: Earliest Ballcourt Is Built
beats.description: Villagers on Mexico's Pacific coast laid out a court for the rubber ball game that later spread across Mesoamerica.
beats.note: Approximate; Paso de la Amada court dated about 1600 BCE

beats.title: Olmec Rise at San Lorenzo
beats.description: The first great Mesoamerican centre grew on the Gulf coast of Mexico, raising colossal stone heads of its rulers.

beats.title: Chavin de Huantar Temple Rises
beats.description: A temple complex of galleries and carved stone heads in the Peruvian Andes became a religious centre across the region.
beats.note: Approximate start of the main temple

beats.title: Zapotecs Found Monte Alban
beats.description: Zapotec leaders levelled a mountaintop in Oaxaca and built a capital with plazas, temples and carved stone slabs.

beats.title: El Mirador Rises as a Maya City
beats.description: A jungle city in Guatemala raised some of the largest pyramids ever built by the Maya.

beats.title: Nazca Lines Are Drawn
beats.description: People of the Peruvian coast scratched huge animals and shapes into the desert floor, visible only from far above.
beats.note: A span of roughly 500 BCE to 500 CE; a middle start year is used

beats.title: Teotihuacan Is Founded
beats.description: A city rose in the Valley of Mexico that would grow into the largest of its age in the Americas.
beats.note: Search: sources range from 400 BCE to 100 BCE; the commonly cited 100 BCE is used

beats.title: Earliest Long Count Date Is Carved
beats.description: A stone monument in Chiapas bore the oldest surviving date in the calendar system later used by the Maya.

beats.title: Pyramid of the Sun Is Built
beats.description: Builders at Teotihuacan raised a vast pyramid of earth and stone along the city's main avenue.
beats.note: Search: ceramics suggest the first or second century CE; some radiocarbon work suggests later. 100 CE used

beats.title: Lord of Sipan Is Buried in Gold
beats.description: A Moche ruler was laid to rest in Peru with gold, turquoise and sacrificed attendants, found intact long afterward.

beats.title: Teotihuacan Conquers Tikal
beats.description: A warlord linked to Teotihuacan arrived at the Maya city, and its king died on the same day.

beats.title: Copan Dynasty Is Founded
beats.description: A new ruler set up a dynasty in a Honduran valley, and his line built one of the great Maya cities.
beats.note: Founding of the dynasty by K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo'

beats.title: Tiwanaku Grows Beside Lake Titicaca
beats.description: A city high in the Andes became the centre of a state with great stone gateways and terraced platforms.

beats.title: Teotihuacan Is Burned
beats.description: Fire swept through the ceremonial heart of Mexico's greatest city, and its power broke for good.

beats.title: Calakmul Defeats Tikal
beats.description: A rival Maya kingdom beat the mighty city of Tikal, which then lost power for more than a century.

beats.title: Wari Empire Spreads in the Andes
beats.description: A highland state built roads and administrative centres across much of Peru, a forerunner of Inca rule.

beats.title: Pakal Takes the Throne at Palenque
beats.description: A twelve-year-old became ruler of a Maya city and went on to rule for nearly seventy years.

beats.title: Pakal Is Sealed in His Tomb
beats.description: The great Maya king was laid in a stone sarcophagus deep inside the Temple of the Inscriptions.

beats.title: Tikal Defeats Calakmul
beats.description: Tikal's king captured the enemy's rulers and began a great revival of the Maya city.

beats.title: Tikal's Temple I Is Raised
beats.description: A soaring pyramid tomb for the victorious Maya king rose over the Guatemalan jungle city's great plaza.
beats.note: Approximate; the king died around 734 and the temple was built after

beats.title: Bonampak Murals Are Painted
beats.description: Maya artists painted vivid scenes of battle, captives and court ceremony on the walls of a small temple.

beats.title: Chan Chan Rises in Coastal Peru
beats.description: The Chimu built a huge adobe capital of walled compounds decorated with fish and bird patterns.

beats.title: Last Classic Maya Date Is Carved
beats.description: A monument at Tonina bore the last Long Count date, as the lowland Maya cities fell silent.

beats.title: Toltecs Found Tollan
beats.description: According to legend, the Toltec people set up their capital in the highlands of central Mexico.

beats.title: Chichen Itza Rises
beats.description: A Maya and Toltec-influenced city on the Yucatan built its great stepped pyramid to the feathered serpent god.
beats.note: Traditional date for the rise of the city

beats.title: Tula Is Burned and Abandoned
beats.description: The Toltec capital's ceremonial heart was burned, ending the power of the highland Mexican state.
beats.note: Search: sources give about 1150 to 1170; 1150 used

beats.title: Cusco Is Founded
beats.description: In Inca legend, the first Sapa Inca chose the valley of Cusco as the site of his people's capital.

beats.title: Acamapichtli Is First Aztec King
beats.description: The people of Tenochtitlan chose a first king, tying their rule to the older line of Culhuacan.
beats.note: Search: one timeline gives 1375; other sources give 1367. 1375 used

beats.title: Aztec Triple Alliance Is Formed
beats.description: Three Mexican cities joined to overthrow their overlord, creating the Aztec Empire.

beats.title: Pachacuti Becomes Inca Ruler
beats.description: After defeating a rival, a new Inca king began turning a small highland state into a vast empire.

beats.title: Moctezuma I Takes the Aztec Throne
beats.description: A warrior king began a long reign in which the Aztec Empire spread far beyond the Valley of Mexico.

beats.title: Mayapan Falls
beats.description: The last great capital of the Yucatan Maya was overthrown and the region split into rival towns.

beats.title: Machu Picchu Is Built
beats.description: Inca builders raised a mountaintop estate of fitted stone high above a river in the Andes.
beats.note: Search: about 1450; a 2023 radiocarbon study suggests construction after about 1420

beats.title: Inca Conquer the Chimu Kingdom
beats.description: Inca armies took the Chimu capital on the Peruvian coast and carried its craftsmen to Cusco.

beats.title: Topa Inca Becomes Sapa Inca
beats.description: A son of Pachacuti took the Inca throne and pushed the empire south into Chile and north into Ecuador.

beats.title: Tenochtitlan Conquers Tlatelolco
beats.description: The Aztec capital attacked and absorbed its twin island city and its great market.

beats.title: Tenochtitlan's Great Temple Opens
beats.description: The Aztecs rededicated their main temple with a ceremony that reportedly lasted several days.

beats.title: Moctezuma II Is Crowned
beats.description: A priest and general became ruler of the Aztec Empire at its greatest extent.
